actual_scope: Sharp two-axis affine/quadratic Gaussian monomial central-quotient kernel cutoff F=6, exact per-residue thresholds and complete test-set criterion, with fixed phase-sign obstruction residuals.
scope_change_reason: The predecessor explicitly asks for least stabilized widths. This bounded two-axis mathematical result is complementary to the live one-axis/general audit and replaces a proof-assistant formalization with a written theorem and exact executable evidence.
bottleneck_link: Finite native identity tests need an exact width contract. This closes the two-axis minimum question and demonstrates phase-affine cancellation invisible through width eight, without asserting a cutoff for the selected nine-axis supplier or changing its paid bill.
stop_rule: Stop after the n=2 necessity/sufficiency proof, sharp residuals, bounded independent checks and portable publication; no n>=3 search, complete native supplier, formal build or selected change.
author: Hiroki KUMAZAKI
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including separate automated mathematical derivation, literal checker and adversarial review subagents in the same session. No independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.

open_questions.question: For n>=3, what is the exact common kernel of phase-fiber pointwise-stabilizer coset-sum representations?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Full-span tuple realization is sufficient in general, but the S4 sign argument making it necessary here does not extend automatically. The exact representation kernel is needed for a minimum cutoff.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one three-axis phase fiber and compute the coset-sum row spaces from all its attainable support stabilizers; distinguish their common kernel from simple affine-span availability.
open_questions.blocked_by: No general-n necessity bridge or minimal-threshold theorem is supplied; a character census alone cannot fill it.
